title: Hitch a trailer: push its CURT ball coupler fully onto the 2 in ball, then latch it, not the other way round
instruction: Hitch the trailer to the ball.
context: Hitching a trailer to a car's tow ball is something most drivers who have rented a U-Haul trailer, towed a boat or a camper, or helped someone else do it, have watched or done. CURT's hook-up guide (curtmfg.com/hooking-trailer): latch up, lower the coupler onto the ball, and "with the coupler fully seated on the ball, engage the latch"; then jack the tongue up to test: "If it comes off the ball, it means that the coupler was not properly seated before being latched." Here the coupler hovers 25 mm over the ball with its handle up. The robot has to push the coupler straight down until the ball seats in the socket, then push the handle down until it latches, driving the underjaw under the ball. Pushed the other way round, the underjaw meets the ball and the handle jams part-way.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the bench top (the station table). A car's back stands at the bench's left end (y 62 on): rear bumper, tailgate, lamps and number plate at real size, cut off at the sides. From the 2 in receiver under its bumper a ball mount runs 40 cm back along -y to a 2 in (50.8 mm) chrome hitch ball at (36, 22), its centre 7 cm above the bench. The trailer's straight tongue runs the other way, along -y, through a tongue jack at y 0 to an A-frame and the front rail and board of a small utility trailer at the bench's right end. On its end is the coupler (modelled on CURT 25153: 27 cm long, 5.2 cm wide, 52.4 mm socket, flared skirt), two safety chains hanging unhooked. At the start the coupler is tipped up 6.5 degrees about the jack, its socket 25 mm above the ball, centred over it; its yellow Posi-Lock handle (5.5 cm) is up at 60 degrees and the red underjaw is retracted.
scoring: Seated: the coupler down within 0.5 degrees and its socket within 1.5 mm of the ball's centre. Latched: the handle within 3 degrees of closed and the underjaw fully in under the ball (within 2 mm of its full 65 mm stroke). At the end: 1.0 once seated and latched, everything at rest and no gripper point within 3 cm of the coupler, for 1 s; 0 whenever the coupler is latched with the ball not seated; 0.5 seated but not latched, at rest for 1 s; 0.25 lowered onto the ball (within 3 degrees) but not seated; 0 otherwise. The score is recomputed from the current state. Real trials: seated is checked as CURT says, by jacking the tongue up (it comes off the ball if it was not seated). The overhead view shows whether the coupler is level and whether the handle is down; the last few millimetres of seating are hidden in the socket.
reset_notes: Lift the coupler back to its stop 25 mm above the ball and raise the handle; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Ball, socket ring and skirt are rigid colliders at real size (2 in ball, 0.4 mm clearance); the coupler is one hinged link pivoting at the jack, light (0.35 kg) so the arm can push it, not a 200 kg tongue. The handle is a hinge; the linkage to the underjaw is a position drive in code, but the jaw is a real slider that hits the ball if not seated. The car, ball mount, jack, trailer front and chains are drawn only, at real size, cut off at the bench.
scores: Scripted (yam_arena, 320x176, seed 1; Brev L40S, 3906c0a, fixture at (36, 22)): demo 1.0 (step 376); naive (handle first, jams; then coupler) 0.5; plate (coupler only) 0.5. Dream-1 flash (seed 1): no score; errored at step 680 (PolicyError: q_r_chunk gripper leaves 0..1).
